title: Hosted API demo - Chat & text generation basics (streaming, params, retries) - Nova Tech
summary: AE/SE run-through of Redwood Hosted API for chat and text generation. Focus on streaming, key generation parameters, retry behavior and best practices. Customer (Nova Tech) is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a product augmentation use case; main concerns are latency SLOs (~200ms), cost, and security/compliance. Agreed to a benchmark session and to share SOC2 and KMS docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Ramos (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mark Sullivan (Nova CTO), Priya Desai (Nova ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (Nova Product)

[00:00] Alicia Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alicia from Redwood Inference, and with me is Jordan our solutions engineer. Um, just checking, everyone can hear ok?
[00:07] Mark Sullivan: Yep, sounds good. Thanks Alicia.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Hi all, quick agenda, we'll do a 20-ish minute hosted API walkthrough, demo streaming and param controls, then a short Q&A and next steps - is that right?
[00:21] Priya Desai: Yep, that works. Our key things: latency targets around 200ms for single-turn chat, cost considerations, and we need to see retry behavior for intermittent network errors.
[00:32] Liam O'Neill: Also curious about console and Optimize suggestions - can Redwood help tune batching/quantization recs?
[00:38] Alicia Ramos: Totally. We'll show the console and the Optimize hints later. Quick qual question - are you currently using an API provider or self-hosting?
[00:45] Mark Sullivan: We're running a mix - some inference in-house on EC2 with Triton, but for new product features we want hosted to shorten time to market. Security is big - SOC2 plus data residency for EU customers.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Got it. Redwood Hosted supports region pinning and we have enterprise docs on SOC2 + audit logs; we'll share those. For the demo I'll use a small chat example.

[02:10] Jordan Lee: (screen share) Ok starting the Hosted API quick demo. Endpoint is /v1/chat/completions, we support streaming via SSE or chunked HTTP. I'll kick off a streaming call, you'll see tokens arrive in real time.
[02:28] Jordan Lee: Example request: messages array with system/user, model param set to redwood-base-2 or similar. Key params: temperature, max_tokens, top_p, frequency_penalty. For deterministic generation we recommend temp=0.
[02:42] Priya Desai: Do you have per-request timeouts or server-side timeouts? If a GPU stalls, how does the client observe that?
[02:50] Jordan Lee: Good q. We have request-level timeouts and advisory SLOs. If a node times out, we return a 504 and include a retry-after header. For streaming specifically, partial chunks may still come and we append final event with status.

[05:05] Jordan Lee: Starting stream now...
[05:12] (streaming tokens)
[05:20] Jordan Lee: You can see tokens coming in every ~50ms here, that's the streaming mode; reduces perceived latency to the user.
[05:32] Mark Sullivan: Nice, that look pretty snappy. What's powering low-latency - batching or model variant?
[05:39] Jordan Lee: A combo - the runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache reuse, plus we have smaller low-latency model variants. For single-turn sub-200ms you might pick a faster variant or tune batch/window. The Console's Optimize tab will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on your traffic.

[08:00] Priya Desai: About params, can we change temperature mid-conversation or per-message?
[08:07] Jordan Lee: Yes, temperature and max_tokens can be set per request; for chat you can set per-message metadata too. We also support function calling and structured output if you need deterministic JSON output.

[10:15] Liam O'Neill: Retries - what are best practices? If we retry a streaming call, do we risk duplication?
[10:24] Jordan Lee: Good point. For non-idempotent generative calls duplication is a risk. We suggest using an idempotency key for at-least-once semantics OR designing client side to detect partial responses and resume. Redwood also supports retry policies in SDKs: exponential backoff and jitter; for streaming we commonly recommend client replay with server-side token offsets when feasible.

[13:40] Mark Sullivan: Any rate limits on hosted tiers, and what does Dedicated change?
[13:48] Alicia Ramos: Hosted has quota and rate limits by plan; Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput for higher SLOs. Most customers start hosted and move to Dedicated if they need strict latency guarantees and isolation.

[16:00] Jordan Lee: I'll show the Console now - dashboard with per-route latency and token cost. Optimize tab suggests batch size, KV cache TTLs, and quantization modes for your model. For example, for your chat loads we might suggest 8-bit quantization and a small batch window to hit your 200ms SLO while saving ~40% per-token cost.
[16:35] Priya Desai: That 40% number - is that based on previous similar workloads?
[16:40] Jordan Lee: It's a projection from our optimizer using similar sequence length distributions; we'll run a bench with your prompt set to get a precise estimate.

[20:05] Mark Sullivan: Security again - how does KMS work? Can we bring our own keys?
[20:12] Alicia Ramos: Yes, BYOK via customer KMS/HSM is supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we integrate with enterprise KMS via our private cluster options and we have encrypted at rest and in transit by default. We'll attach the SOC2 + KMS whitepaper after the call.

[23:00] Priya Desai: For benchmarking, our biggest worry is p95 latency under load; can you run a sample bench and show us p50/p95 and token cost?
[23:10] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll schedule a benchmark session; Jordan will lead it and Alicia will coordinate access and keys. We'll ask you to provide a representative prompt set and target latency/cost goals.

[26:30] Liam O'Neill: Any caveats on streaming for mobile clients? Intermittent network makes chunk ordering tricky.
[26:38] Jordan Lee: For mobile, we recommend small chunks + reconnect heuristics. The SDKs include helpers to resume streams and dedupe tokens; again idempotency keys help for replay scenarios.

[29:50] Mark Sullivan: Competitors - how does Redwood compare to OpenAI or Anthropic for hosted?
[29:58] Alicia Ramos: We focus on production economics - unified tooling for hosted/dedicated/private, plus Optimize and workload-aware batching. In many cases latency/cost beats managed endpoints because of our kernel selection and continuous batching. We'll avoid overclaiming though; we'll share benchmarks and you can run your own.

[33:00] Priya Desai: Quick question on SDK retries and error codes, what should we handle client-side vs server-side?
[33:08] Jordan Lee: Handle network and 5xx with retry/backoff. For 4xx, surface to user or fail fast. We also return structured error codes in the payload; SDKs translate common ones.

[36:20] Alicia Ramos: Ok to recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2 and KMS docs, schedule a benchmarking session (Jordan to run), share pricing tiers and expected cost delta for quantization. Can we target next week for bench setup?
[36:35] Mark Sullivan: Next week works, Priya will send prompt set and rough traffic profile.
[36:42] Priya Desai: Yup, I'll upload the prompts and a small sample dataset.
[36:47] Liam O'Neill: And send your console screenshots and the Optimize example.

[38:00] Alicia Ramos: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an invite for the bench and attach the security docs.
[38:08] Meeting ends with brief goodbyes and some cross-chat as people drop off.
next_steps: Alicia to send SOC2 and KMS whitepaper
Jordan to schedule and run benchmarking session with Nova prompt set
Priya to upload representative prompt set and traffic profile
Alicia to share pricing tiers and quantization cost estimates
